newsitem.title: UK: Major reaffirms he wants May 1 British election.
newsitem.headline: Major reaffirms he wants May 1 British election.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major made clear to his ministers on Monday that he does not want to go to the polls before May 1.
Conservative Party sources said Major reaffirmed the date at the start of a cabinet meeting at his official country home Chequers to consider proposals for the party's election manifesto.

"I think you will see a manifesto that is full of exciting ideas, that is a people-centred manifesto and that carries forward the opportunity revolution this government has put in place," Conservative chairman Brian Mawhinney told BBC radio.
"We want to make sure this country becomes the enterprise centre of Europe. We want to develop, build on what we have already put in place," Mawhinney added.

Recent polls have shown the Conservatives trailing some 20 points behind the opposition Labour Party. An election could be held as late as May 22 but the media has speculated that Major could set an election date in April or even March.
A May date would allow time for a by-election in late February or early March in Wirral South, near the north-western port of Liverpool.
Opinion polls suggest Labour will win the seat, which would put the Conservatives in a minority of one in the House of Commons.
Critics say the Conservatives have run out of ideas after almost 18 years in power.

British newspapers speculated that proposals under discussion would include moves to raise billions of pounds (dollars) by selling off government property, buildings and state agencies such as the benefits agency and national savings.
They also suggested there could be important promises on education, possibly including the removal of local authority control over state schools.
